note: Batch B7 — HU 40bb SRP from the flop; OOP (BB) facing the third barrel, the most common river decision in practice. BB check, BTN c-bet flop, BB call; BB check, BTN barrel turn, BB call; river BB check, BTN bets 50%, and BB decides fold/call/raise. Extracted node is nodePlayer=0 (OOP) facing a bet; export sets facing=singleRaise, heroSeatOffsetFromButton=1 (BB). Same 4 boards/cards as the betting-line batch, whose river node was BB acting unopened — this is the same line one action deeper. Partial-independence: the BTN river bet sizing is fixed OUTSIDE the verified subtree (weaker on the bettor side), earlier streets solver-self-reported + byte-reproducible — disclosed on the content. Solved harder than the shallower batches (target 0.001 vs 0.002, maxIterations bounded at 1000): this is the deepest line in the set (three streets of betting), so its river node is reached rarely and the 0.002 target left the local river subtree ~0.3% of pot exploitable — 2-6x worse than every other batch. Note the solver stops as soon as the target is met, so the shallower batches only ever ran a couple hundred iterations; iteration count, bounded by maxIterations, is the real precision knob here (an unbounded 10000-iteration attempt cost ~4h per spot and was abandoned).
